headlines.text: It was 2023 when it was title-change night as Eddie Kingston (the NJPW STRONG Openweight Champion) vs. Claudio Castagnoli battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.18 ? a genuinely great match ? ending the champion's reign. In a title-for-title match built on years of history dating back to their indie days, Kingston finally beat Castagnoli with a spinning back fist and powerbomb to become ROH World Champion.

Back on this day in 2025, Brodido vs. JetSpeed vs. Alexander & Hechicero vs. The Young Bucks clashed for the AEW World Tag Team Titles in a Ladder match, appearing on All Out, rated 8.28 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. It was the first title opportunity of Alexander & Hechicero's career. Brodido survived a four-way ladder war against the Young Bucks, JetSpeed and the Don Callis Family to retain the AEW World Tag Team Titles.
That Friday in 2024, Hikaru Shida vs. Harley Cameron met for the very first time on Rampage, rated 5.74.

secondaries.text: That Saturday in 2025, the AEW Unified Title was up for grabs as Kazuchika Okada vs. Konosuke Takeshita vs. Mascara Dorada went to war, appearing on All Out, rated 9.10 ? an incredible outing. Okada dropkicked Takeshita out of the ring before hitting a Rainmaker on Dorada to retain the Unified Championship, as tension within the Don Callis Family boiled over.

2025 brought us this moment: the AEW Women's World Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Kris Statlander vs. Toni Storm vs. Jamie Hayter vs. Thekla battled it out, appearing on All Out, rated 6.83 ? ending the champion's reign at 6 defenses. It was the first title opportunity of Thekla's career. Statlander hooked Storm's limbs for a seatbelt pin to dethrone her in a four-way, becoming a new AEW Women's World Champion.

On a Saturday in 2025, back when Adam Page vs. Kyle Fletcher fought tooth and nail for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on All Out, rated 9.27 ? a war that left everything in the ring. Page survived Fletcher borrowing Ospreay's Hidden Blade in a 38-minute classic to retain the AEW World Championship.
